system_overview: This specification models the voucher cancellation operation, implemented using the Two-Phase Commit protocol. A Voucher Transaction Provider coordinates voucher holders and voucher issuers to atomically cancel previously issued vouchers. This operation is an addendum to RFC 3506 and is not described in the original RFC.
actors_and_components: Four types of participants interact: (1) A Voucher Transaction Provider (the coordinator) managing the commit/abort decision. (2) Voucher Holders who currently hold the vouchers. (3) Voucher Issuers who originally issued the vouchers. (4) The vouchers themselves, which transition from valid to cancelled. Communication uses a shared message pool where messages accumulate and are never removed.
state_variables: The system tracks seven pieces of state: (1) each voucher's current status (valid or cancelled), (2) each voucher's lifecycle phase (working or done), (3) each holder's participation state (holding, prepared, cancelled, or aborted), (4) each issuer's participation state (waiting, prepared, cancelled, or aborted), (5) the coordinator's state (initial or done), (6) the set of participants from which the coordinator has received cancellation preparation confirmations, and (7) the pool of all messages sent.
initial_state: All vouchers are in the valid state with lifecycle in the working phase (since cancellation presupposes a previously issued voucher). All holders are in the holding state. All issuers are in the waiting state. The coordinator is in the initial state with empty preparation confirmations and empty message pool.
actions: The coordinator can: receive preparation confirmations from a holder and an issuer, cancel a voucher (transitioning it to cancelled and lifecycle to done, enabled only when all participants have prepared), or spontaneously abort. Each holder can: prepare for cancellation (sending a preparation message), spontaneously abort, receive a cancellation message (transitioning to cancelled state), or receive an abort message (transitioning to aborted state). Each issuer can: prepare, spontaneously abort, receive a cancellation message (transitioning to cancelled), or receive an abort message (transitioning to aborted).
safety_properties: Type correctness ensures all variables remain in expected domains. A consistency invariant ensures no holder and issuer reach conflicting decisions: a holder must not be cancelled while an issuer is aborted, and a holder must not be aborted while an issuer is cancelled.
model_bounds: The model-checking configuration uses three vouchers, three holders, and three issuers. Deadlock checking is disabled.
additional_assumptions: The specification imports and claims to implement the voucher lifecycle specification as a refinement. Messages are modeled as a growing set that is never consumed. Preparation messages from the coordinator are not explicitly modeled. The cancellation operation requires the voucher to be in the valid/working state, meaning it must have been previously issued.
